- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the next few days; apply a downward correction of 5–10% for the immediate follow-up period.
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >10% over 3–5 days), check sentiment for bullish bias — if present, consider mean reversion or reduce forecast by 2–5% per day.
- If model forecast is significantly below true outcome (e.g., >10% under 3–5 days), check sentiment for bearish bias — if present, consider mean reversion or increase forecast by 2–5% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-stage sentiment-driven surges; add a 1–3 day lag correction if sentiment turns bullish after day 15–20.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag — adjust forecast to align with sentiment direction 2–3 days ahead.
